public_sources.title: PACE: Anytime-Valid Acceptance Tests for Self-Evolving Agents
public_sources.used_scope: Self-evolving agents repeatedly propose edits and compare candidates to incumbents on identical instances using a testing-by-betting e-process. The public abstract states a per-decision false-commit guarantee under optional stopping; used as the direct agent-acceptance baseline, not as a theorem for adaptive same-dev candidate generation across a whole loop.

public_sources.title: What Fits (Into Few Tokens) Doesn't Overfit: Compression and Generalization in ML Research Agents
public_sources.authors: Martin Andres Bertran; Aaron Roth; Zhiwei Steven Wu
public_sources.used_scope: Explorer proposes h_t adaptively from a one-bit running-best transcript; descriptions/decoders are fixed before validation and statements condition on randomness independent of validation. Its ladder bound counts possible improvement-location transcripts; used to justify treating the full counterfactual validation transcript as a selection object and to preserve an independence gate for learned priors.

public_sources.title: On the role of data in PAC-Bayes bounds
public_sources.authors: Gintare Karolina Dziugaite; Kyle Hsu; Waseem Gharbieh; Gabriel Arpino; Daniel M. Roy
public_sources.used_scope: Shows that a prior may be learned from a subset that is then excluded from the empirical-risk term. Used as supporting precedent for disjoint prior-building data; the exact weighted-e validity below is derived directly by conditioning and does not rely on PAC-Bayes.

public_sources.title: Family-wise Error Rate Control with E-values
public_sources.used_scope: Develops FWER control with e-values and weighted averages of e-values, including sequential/anytime-valid properties. Used as external support that fixed weighted e-combinations are a legitimate design primitive; the selected-transcript/fresh-audit construction below is worker-local.

disjoint_learned_transcript_prior_validi.statement: Let Z be prior-building data independent of the reused validation data D. Conditional on Z, let pi_Z(u)>=0 sum to <=1 over all counterfactual transcript/test opportunities u. For each fixed u, let E_{u,t}(D) be a valid e-process under its null. Then P(exists u,t: E_{u,t} >= 1/(alpha*pi_Z(u)) | Z) <= sum_u alpha*pi_Z(u) <= alpha by Ville plus union bound. Integrating over Z preserves the same bound.
disjoint_learned_transcript_prior_validi.consequence: Mixture weights/codebooks may be fit arbitrarily on genuinely disjoint meta-data and then frozen. No extra penalty is needed merely because the learned prior is random before conditioning; leakage from the current reused validation channel invalidates this argument.
disjoint_learned_transcript_prior_validi.scope_guard: Requires the counterfactual decoder/candidate mapping and learned prior to be fixed conditional on Z before seeing current D, and fixed-u e-process validity to hold.

selected_transcript_global_evalue.statement: For realized transcript U(D), define S(D)=pi(U)*E_U(D), with pi fixed independently of D and each fixed candidate/transcript e-value satisfying E[E_u]<=1. Then E[S] = sum_u pi(u) E[E_u 1{U=u}] <= sum_u pi(u) E[E_u] <= 1.
selected_transcript_global_evalue.consequence: The usual transcript-weighted threshold E_U >= 1/(alpha*pi(U)) is equivalent to testing the single global selected e-value S>=1/alpha. This representation makes safe combination with a fresh audit possible.

hard_switch_full_alpha_is_not_generally_.statement: A validation-dependent hard choice between two level-alpha procedures cannot in general give each branch the full alpha. Counterexample: let A be the reuse-test rejection event with P(A)=alpha; choose reuse iff A occurs, otherwise run an independent fresh level-alpha test B. Then false rejection is P(A)+P(A^c)P(B)=alpha+(1-alpha)alpha=2alpha-alpha^2, which is 0.0975 at alpha=.05.
hard_switch_full_alpha_is_not_generally_.safe_fallback: A hard switch can use alpha_r+alpha_f<=alpha (or another proven branch-spending rule), but this may reduce power. Do not interpret 'fresh audit on high-complexity paths' plus 'reuse test on low-complexity paths' as automatically level-alpha when both use full alpha.

fresh_reuse_convex_eprocess.setup: After adaptive development on D, form selected-transcript global e-value S. Freeze the selected candidate. On an independent fresh audit stream A_1,A_2,... construct a conditional e-process F_t for that fixed selected candidate, with F_0=1 and E[F_t | D,A_{<t}] <= F_{t-1} under the global null that every selectable candidate is null.
fresh_reuse_convex_eprocess.construction: For fixed lambda in [0,1] independent of current D/audit, define H_0=lambda*S+(1-lambda) and H_t=lambda*S+(1-lambda)*F_t for t>=1.
fresh_reuse_convex_eprocess.validity: E[H_0]<=1 because E[S]<=1. Conditional on D, H_t is a nonnegative supermartingale over the fresh audit because S is constant and F_t is a conditional e-process. Therefore the two-stage process starting before D is an e-process and P(sup_t H_t >= 1/alpha)<=alpha.
fresh_reuse_convex_eprocess.cost_property: If H_0 already exceeds 1/alpha, commit without fresh audit; otherwise collect fresh audit sequentially and stop on crossing or budget exhaustion. This gives an audit-on-demand mechanism without a data-dependent full-alpha branch switch.
fresh_reuse_convex_eprocess.learned_lambda: lambda may itself be selected using disjoint prior-building/meta-simulation data Z; conditional on Z it is fixed, so the same validity proof applies.
fresh_reuse_convex_eprocess.scope_guard: Requires fresh audit independence/conditional validity for the selected candidate and a global null over selectable candidates. It does not by itself provide selective effect estimation after rejection.

worker_local_full_loop_simulator.purpose: Stress-test selection correction and fresh-audit designs in a stylized validation-dependent proposal loop; not a claim about any deployed agent.
worker_local_full_loop_simulator.runs: Typically 60k-80k Monte Carlo trajectories per reported N/condition; 50 repeats for prior-learning sample-size summaries.

proposal_loop.feedback: One bit after each proposal beyond the first: 1 iff that candidate's reused-dev fixed-horizon paired-sign e-value is a new record.
proposal_loop.validation_dependent_generation_alternat: At proposal t, genuine-good probability is min(0.02+0.10*r_history,0.45), where r_history is the number of previous record-improvement bits. Genuine-good candidates have discordant win probability q=.75; all other candidates q=.5.
proposal_loop.null: All selectable candidates have discordant win probability q=.5 regardless of history.
proposal_loop.paired_sign_evalue: Per independent task: concordant factor 1 with probability 1-rho, discordant candidate win factor 1.5, discordant incumbent win factor 0.5; rho=.4. Reused-dev selection uses final fixed-horizon e-values to isolate cross-candidate adaptivity; fresh-audit comparisons below use the actual running fresh e-process for optional stopping.
proposal_loop.selected_candidate: Highest reused-dev final e-value among proposals seen before stop. This is deliberately selection-biased under the null.

disjoint_prior_learning.model_components: flat fallback plus fast/medium/slow transcript models from the previous checkpoint; final learned prior reserves at least 0.10 mass for flat by mixing 0.10*flat + 0.90*EM-fit.
disjoint_prior_learning.interpretation: Under this particular simulated loop, disjoint meta-data recovers nearly all of the available code-length gain by about M=200, but the absolute gain over equal mix4 is only ~0.12 bit. Prior learning is validity-safe under the independence condition; whether it is worthwhile is an empirical utility question.

fixed_convex_eprocess_audit_cost_result.disjoint_tuning: A grid over lambda was tuned only on separate simulated meta-runs, not the reported evaluation trajectories. With a utility that strongly penalized false/harmful commits, lambda=0 was selected for N<=100 and lambda=.2 for N=200.
fixed_convex_eprocess_audit_cost_result.interpretation: At N=200, a small independently tuned reuse contribution reduced mean fresh-audit work by ~5.3 tasks (~4.1%), slightly increased true commits, and lowered false commits in this simulation. At N<=100 the tuned lambda collapsed to zero: the transcript complexity penalty made reuse evidence too weak to help. This is a finite-simulation utility result, not a theorem that lambda=.2 is optimal elsewhere.

measurement_warnings: Naive same-dev acceptance can be anti-conservative after adaptive candidate selection even when every fixed candidate e-value is valid; the N50 null false-commit rate was ~8.9% in this stylized loop.
Selection-corrected reuse can become extremely conservative at short horizons because transcript complexity raises the threshold; this is a power cost, not a validity failure.
Fresh-audit and reuse evidence should not be joined by an uncorrected validation-dependent hard switch with full alpha in both branches.

The simulator uses fixed-horizon reused-dev candidate e-values and independent task outcomes conditional on candidate class; candidate correlations, task heterogeneity, and within-candidate dev optional stopping remain future stress tests.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Fit transcript-mixture weights/codebook parameters on disjoint prior-building meta-data, freeze them, then use the learned prior in transcript-weighted e-certificates.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct conditional weighted-Ville derivation plus worker-local heldout coding simulation; PAC-Bayes split-prior literature is supporting precedent.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: No current-validation leakage into prior fitting. If meta-data overlap or are adaptively chosen using current validation, another correction is required.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Represent adaptive selection correction as the single e-value S=pi(U)E_U, rather than only as a moving threshold.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Direct expectation inequality over counterfactual transcript opportunities.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Requires fixed-u e-value validity and pi independent of current validation.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Treat a data-dependent reuse-vs-fresh branch choice as a multiple-testing object. Full alpha in both branches can reach 2alpha-alpha^2 in a simple counterexample.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Does not say every practical switch inflates error; it rejects the unconditional claim that such switching is automatically level-alpha.

new_or_updated_candidate_findings.mechanism: Combine selected transcript-weighted reuse e-value S with an independent fresh audit e-process F_t using fixed/disjoint-learned lambda: H_t=lambda S+(1-lambda)F_t; collect audit only until H crosses or the audit budget ends.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.evidence: Worker-local two-stage supermartingale derivation plus full-loop simulation showing a modest N=200 audit-cost gain at lambda=.2.
new_or_updated_candidate_findings.scope_guard: Fresh audit must be conditionally valid/independent after candidate freeze; lambda cannot be tuned on the same current validation path without an additional argument.

rejected_or_narrowed_generalizations: Rejected: 'a hard complexity-based switch can use alpha=.05 for reuse and alpha=.05 for fresh because only one branch executes.' Selection of the branch can itself couple to rejection risk.
Rejected: 'learning a better transcript prior from any historical-looking data is free.' It is free only under a defensible independence/conditioning boundary or another theorem controlling leakage.

Narrowed: 'nonuniform prior learning will materially restore short-horizon power.' In the full-loop simulation the learned prior saved only ~0.12 bit on average versus equal mix4 and weighted reuse remained almost powerless below 100 tasks.

Narrowed: 'combining reuse and fresh evidence always saves audit.' Independently tuned lambda was zero at N<=100 in the reported simulator; useful blending appeared only at N=200 under the chosen meta-distribution.

frontier.action: Derive or locate a safe complexity-dependent e-merging/allocation rule that permits lambda or fresh-audit allocation to depend on the current transcript complexity without paying a crude alpha split; compare to fixed-lambda convex e-process and alpha-spent hard switching.

Stress the full adaptive loop across q in {0.60,0.65,0.70,0.75,0.80}, discordance in {0.2,0.4,0.6}, fresh-audit budgets 20-200, and learned-prior sample sizes 20-1000; report true commit, harmful/false commit, unresolved rate, and audit tasks.

Replace reused-dev final e-values with actual within-candidate anytime PACE paths while retaining cross-candidate transcript selection; verify that the selected-global-evalue construction remains valid when each E_u is a supremum/e-process certificate.

Introduce shared task difficulty and cross-candidate correlated outcomes on the reused dev set, plus task-cluster dependence, to test power/robustness of transcript correction without changing the exact fixed-u validity assumptions.

Compare disjoint learned mixture priors against validation-independent language-model/prefix priors and exact behavior-equivalence aggregation; measure bits saved per added prior-building sample and sensitivity to meta-distribution shift.

exact_next_action: Search e-value/e-process merging literature for conditions under which current-data-dependent weights are safe, then derive a complexity-adaptive fresh/reuse combiner or prove a lower-bound/necessity of extra spending; in parallel run the q/rho/audit-budget grid for the fixed-lambda construction.
